import statistics, math
# CCSA from DOL Sep 10 table, thousands
vals = [1875,1865,1823,1842,1859,1865,1827,1871,1847,1851,1816,1832,1787,1809,1808,1776,1758,1776,1771,1785,1771,1786,1800,1812,1806,1821,1798,1789,1777,1799,1781,1796,1771,1775,1774]
# dates Jan 3 to Aug 29. compute changes sigma all 2026 and maybe recent since Mar14 or June
changes=[vals[i]-vals[i-1] for i in range(1,len(vals))]
for start_idx,name in [(0,'all Jan-Aug'),(10,'Mar14-Aug'),(22,'Jun6-Aug'),(25,'Jul-Aug')]:
    ch=[vals[i]-vals[i-1] for i in range(max(1,start_idx),len(vals))]
    print(name, len(ch), 'mean', statistics.mean(ch), 'stdev', statistics.stdev(ch), 'h3 sigma', statistics.stdev(ch)*math.sqrt(3), 'hw', statistics.stdev(ch)*math.sqrt(3)*1.28)
# three-week changes for same horizon maybe as in prior used three-week change volatility
ch3=[vals[i]-vals[i-3] for i in range(3,len(vals))]
for start_idx,name in [(0,'all 3wk'),(10,'Mar14 3wk'),(22,'Jun6 3wk')]:
    c=[vals[i]-vals[i-3] for i in range(max(3,start_idx),len(vals))]
    print(name, len(c), statistics.mean(c), statistics.stdev(c), 'hw', statistics.stdev(c)*1.28)
print(changes)
print(ch3[-12:])
PY"
